newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline firm on crude gains, healthy demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline firm on crude gains, healthy demand.

text.p: NWE gasoline was firmer on Monday in line with crude gains on Friday, healthy local demand and the re-opening of the arbitrage door to the U.S. traders said.
Eurograde barges traded at between $208 to $209.50 a tonne fob ARA throughout the day although trade was subdued by the absence of many key players due to public holidays across most of Europe.

"The early trades were probably just done to bump up the posted prices but I think it's fair given the gains seen in crude," said one broker. "You have to be getting at least $208 to make it work given the strength in crude."

Traders said the market was in for a busy week, with plenty of demand seen from Britain where oil companies are trying to stock up ahead of possible tax hikes by the new Labour government in its post-election budget.
The re-opening of the arbitrage door to the U.S. was also expected to draw material out of the region, potentially tightening supply.
There was a price differential of roughly $26 between Eurograde fob barges and NYMEX June unleaded and $23 against the July contract late on Monday.
